title: Perfect Completeness of the Split Character Tester
statement: Let $H$ be a subspace of the binary cube $\ bf_2^n$, and let a split identify that cube linearly with $H\times\bbf_2^k$, carrying $(h,0)$ to $h$. For $x,y\in\bbf_2^k$ and $h\in H$, consider the three points corresponding to $(h,x)$, $(0,y)$, and $(0,x+y)$; the tester samples $(x,y,h)$ uniformly and accepts exactly when the product of the first two function values equals the third. Every function of the form $z\mapsto(-1)^{\langle\gamma,\pi_2(\Phi^{-1}z)\rangle}$, for some $\gamma\in\bbf_2^k$, is accepted with probability $1$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $n$ and a subspace $H\leq\bbf_2^n$
